content: The GraphLike proposals I've seen in Mathlib are #36743 and #39586.

Recent discussion happening here: #graph theory > HasAdj
It seems the main issue is making sure we support hypergraphs

Note that @Jun Kwon has laid out a roadmap explaining the plan when others can start contributing

https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/252551-graph-theory/topic/Formalization.20of.20tree.20decompositions/near/593830719
3 messages were moved here from #CSLib > Online Meetings by Chris Henson.
(moved to keep the meeting thread uncluttered)

For those not in the meeting, we were discussing this as a way to keep Mathlib and CSLib aligned on their treatment of graphs. I feel very strongly that we do not duplicate definitions of graphs from Mathlib, and think this work could help.

One claim I have is that a single GraphLike class is not very useful, as this isn't really any different to having a CanonicalGraph structure and writing Digraph.toCanonicalGraph, SimpleGraph.toCanonicalGraph etc, and doing everything in terms of CanonicalGraph
The reason that docs#SetLike and docs#FunLike are useful is because we have additional typeclasses that attach extra properties, like docs#AddMonoidHomClass

Eric Wieser said:

One claim I have is that a single GraphLike class is not very useful, as this isn't really any different to having a CanonicalGraph structure and writing Digraph.toCanonicalGraph, SimpleGraph.toCanonicalGraph etc, and doing everything in terms of CanonicalGraph

(Outsider from the mathlib discussion, so I might imagine things here:)
Shouldn't the idea be to have several GraphLike classes, like GraphLike.Directed, GraphLike.Undirected, GraphLike.LabelledDirected, etc.?

This is exactly what is proposed in the roadmap.
